before_item.title: The Alexander polynomial does not determine the prime knot summands

references.title: Burde and Zieschang, Knots, 2nd revised and extended edition
references.locator: Chapter 7, §§7.6–7.7 and §15.4, printed pp.94 and 254; granny and square knots

before_item.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For an oriented Seifert surface $F\subset S^3$ with boundary $K$ and ordered basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, let $V$ be the Seifert matrix with entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Here $\operatorname{lk}$ is the integer linking number of disjoint oriented cycles in $S^3$, and $a_i^+$ is a small push-off in the positive normal direction, chosen so that the positive normal followed by the oriented basis of $F$ gives the orientation of $S^3$. Use the standard knot-invariant conventions $\Delta_K(t)=\det(V-tV^T)$ up to units $\pm t^k$ and $\sigma_{-1}(K)=\operatorname{sign}(2(V+V^T))$, where the matrix sign is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues; independence of the chosen surface and basis is part of the Seifert-form invariance theorems. Let $T$ be the standard right-handed trefoil, let $T^*$ be its image under a fixed orientation-reversing reflection of $S^3$, and let $-T^*$ be that image with reversed knot orientation. Define $G=T\#T$ and $Q=T\#(-T^*)$. Then $\Delta_G(t)\doteq\Delta_Q(t)\doteq(t^2-t+1)^2$, and $|\sigma_{-1}(G)|=4$ while $\sigma_{-1}(Q)=0$. The oriented prime-factor multisets of $G$ and $Q$ are different. Thus equality of Alexander polynomials does not determine the prime knot summands.
